question: Is CFTR specifically enriched in ductal cells?

plan.interpreted_question: Is CFTR (HGNC:1884; ENSG00000001626) specifically enriched in ductal cells, i.e., GENE_ENRICHED_IN ductal anatomical structures versus other cell types in the graph?

graph_answer:
Yes. In PanKgraph, CFTR (HGNC:1884; ENSG00000001626) has recorded GENE_ENRICHED_IN evidence for ductal populations only. The two matching enrichment records are for ductal cell (CL_0002079) and pancreatic ductal cell MUC5B+ (CL_0002079_MUC5B) [G1]. The query for all CFTR enrichment targets returned no other cell types [G1].

| Cell type | log2 fold change | padj | % cells expressing | Condition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ductal cell (CL_0002079) | 7.62 | 2.7e-195 | 87.3 | ND |
| MUC5B+ ductal (CL_0002079_MUC5B) | 1.23 | 0.0147 | 61.2 | ND |

Both records are positive one-versus-rest comparisons with an "Expressed" call [G1]. Each target cell type was compared with the remaining cell types in the source analysis. Source: PanKgraph_08_04, DE methods data version 2026-04-01 [G1].

**Interpretation.** Enrichment means higher expression in the target cell type than in the other cell types in the source analysis. The effect is far stronger in ductal cells than in the MUC5B+ subtype. This is recorded enrichment, not an annotated marker-gene relationship, and it does not establish exclusive expression. The execution coverage for this query was not formally verified as complete, so "no other cell types" reflects the returned records rather than an exhaustive-absence claim.

**Terminology.** MUC5B+ ductal cells are a study-specific subtype within the ductal-cell category. This subtype has no public ontology term of its own yet (its identifier carries a local suffix).
